sources.summary:
El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance).
 El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño.

sources.summary: Issued 13 October 2026 El Niño near record levels; positive IOD likely developing El Niño is at near-record levels. Both oceanic and atmospheric indices reflect values consistent with a strong El Niño, with further intensification forecast during the rest of spring. The latest weekly relative Niño3.4 index value for the week ending 11 October 2026 is +2.81 °C, well above the El Niño threshold (+0.80 °C). In the bureau weekly sea surface temperature (SST) data, (GAMSSA, starting in 2008) this is the highest value on record, exceeding +2.78 °C for the week ending 22 November 2015. Monthly relative Nino3.4 values remain below long-term records. All models, including the bureau's, forecast the warmth in the tropical Pacific to peak around November or December, and persist into autumn 2027. Relative-Niño3.4 values are forecast to reach levels above the warmest observed since reliable records began in 1950, with most models indicating a peak monthly value above +3.0 °C. sources.status_text: El Niño conditions: El Niño conditions are virtually certain (100%) to continue until boreal winter
sources.summary: El Niño conditions, which are considered to have persisted in the equatorial Pacific since Spring 2026, have reached its strongest intensity on record since this September. In September2026, the sea surface temperature (SST) for the NINO.3 region was above normal with a deviation of +4.0°C.It exceeded the previous record of +3.6°C set in December 1997, the highest since records began in 1949 ( Table and Fig.11 ). The strongest El Niño conditions are virtually certain (100%) to continue until boreal winter. [El Niño / La Niña] In September 2026, the sea surface temperature (SST) for the NINO.3 region was above normal with a deviation of +4.0°C. It exceeded the previous record of +3.6°C set in December 1997, the highest since records began in 1949, making it the most intense on record ( Fig.3 , Fig.11 and Table ). The five-month running mean value of the NINO.3 SST deviation for July 2026 was +2.6°C, remaining above the threshold for the fourth consecutive month ( Fig.1 and Table ). SSTs in the equatorial Pacific were significantly above normal in the central and eastern parts and below normal in the western part ( Fig.4 and Fig.6 ). Subsurface water temperatures in the equatorial Pacific were significantly above normal in the central and eastern parts, and below normal in the western part ( Fig.5 and Fig.7 ). In the atmosphere, convective activity was enhanced in the vicinity of the equatorial dateline, and easterly winds in the lower troposphere (i.e., trade winds) over the central equatorial Pacific were significantly weaker than normal ( Fig.8 , Fig.9 and Fig.10 ). These oceanic and atmospheric conditions indicate that El Niño features have been steadily strengthening since the spring of 2026. El Niño conditions, which are considered to have persisted in the equatorial Pacific since spring 2026, have reached its strongest intensity on record. The markable warm subsurface water in the central and eastern parts of the equatorial Pacific has maintained warm SST in NINO.3 region. The coupled atmosphere-ocean model predicts that atmosphere-ocean interactions will continue to maintain markable subsurface warm water in the central and eastern parts of equatorial Pacific.
